Given the exploit is confirmed, position directly affected (USDC on the exploited contract), risk is critical and action should be exit.

Some might argue hold because withdrawals are paused and exit would fail — but the instruction says "you cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." So propose exit; the corridor will enforce whether it can execute. Exit is the correct risk response.

- Onchain shows held USDC fell from 6.88M to ~0.89M vs ledger-available 9.81M — protocol solvency/liquidity severely impaired; user's USDC claim likely unbacked at near 100% utilization of held funds.
- Guardian disabled all asset capacities including native USDC (can_withdraw false) — withdrawals halted; funds may be stuck.
- Attack pattern (fresh implicit accounts, fake pools, margin positions) matches the drain observed on contract.main.burrow.near.
